paragraphs: Rav Akavya: Rava asks who else was wise enough for the great cauldron, Pesaḥim. Not there, but Avodah Zarah 76b: Rav Akavya fitted the cauldron with a dough rim (gadanfa); Rava praised his wisdom. Arukh reads Rav Ukva. Perhaps the error arose from Bava Metzia 70a, where the cauldron of Mar Ukva’s sons was weighed before it was lent out. But Tosafot Shabbat 42b cites Mar Ukva buying a gentile's cauldron and making the rim, following Arukh's reading. Arukh has Rav Ukva, Tosafot Mar Ukva, which troubles me as discussed there. Tosafot Nazir 53a likewise places Mar Ukva in Rava's time; see his entry.
